clue.text: Admits recasting is central to …

indicators.note: recasting a play or a metal object reshapes it, so the letters of the word admits are given a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a change of actors lies at the heart of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next one, where 'central to' does a second job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amidst others sits in their middle, so the preposition means at the heart of them.

clue.text: … all-father in German operas

indicators.note: the ellipsis carries on from the clue before, whose words 'central to' show that the answer sits in the middle of the following words

explanation.surface: Wotan, the all-father of Norse myth, is central to a famous cycle of German operas.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator comes from 1 Down: read the two clues as one, '… is central to … all-father in German', and the answer sits inside 'all-father in German'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's four-opera cycle, Der Ring des Nibelungen, is known in English simply as The Ring; it is also where boxers fight.

clue.text: Knockout set up by this person in storm of major frenzies?

definitions.text: Knockout set up by this person in storm of major frenzies?

indicators.note: in places the reversed knockout and the pronoun inside the jumbled letters
a storm throws things about wildly, so the letters of major frenzies are scattered into a new order
in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: KO is the standard boxing abbreviation for a knockout
the setter speaking of themselves is I

explanation.surface: A boxer describes landing a knockout amid a great frenzy of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the knockout abbreviation, as this is a down clue. Frazier floored Ali in the fifteenth round of their 1971 fight, so the whole clue also describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokin' Joe Frazier was the heavyweight champion who beat Ali in 1971, famous for a crushing left hook.

clue.text: See 21
Thus far, one's own source of mischief

parts.note: on one's tod is British slang for alone, from rhyming slang Tod Sloan for own, so tod stands for own
Ate is the Greek goddess who embodies mischief and ruin, the source of it

explanation.surface: So far, a person's own doings have been the root of all the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: TOD comes from the British rhyming slang 'on your Tod (Sloan)', meaning on your own.
explanation.definitionFit: To date means up to the present moment, the same as so far or until now.

clue.text: Time the broken urinal's fixed, man wanting to do one

indicators.note: fixed in place means the reduced word is set inside the jumbled letters
a broken thing is in pieces, so the letters of urinal are put back in a new order
wanting means lacking, so the word for a man is taken away from the

parts.note: taken as written
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A plumber mends a broken urinal, then a man wants to get out of there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges URINAL as URNAIL, and 'fixed' sets the lone T inside it. 'Do one' is British slang for clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is to run away, and the British slang 'do one' also means leave quickly.

clue.text: A number of apostles contemplate their essence?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to practise the Japanese Buddhist meditation that seeks the essence of things

explanation.surface: Followers of a faith meditate on what lies at their very core.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer 2,3 as DO ZEN, to practise Zen; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles numbered twelve, and a dozen is a set of twelve.

clue.text: 21 16 vs 3, through fifteen tetchy rounds

indicators.note: rounding up or going round turns things over, so the letters of through fifteen tetchy are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two boxers slug it out bad-temperedly over fifteen rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 Down's light is THE and 16 Down's is GREATEST, so '21 16 vs 3' is The Greatest (Ali) against Smokin' Joe Frazier. 'Rounds' looks like the boxing term but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali against Frazier at Madison Square Garden in March 1971 was billed as the Fight of the Century.

clue.text: One's not very good at boxing in silence (something bizarre to behold!)

definitions.text: One's not very good at boxing in silence (something bizarre to behold!)

indicators.note: in places the poor performer inside the word for silence

parts.note: mum is silence, as in keeping mum

parts.words: One's not very good at boxing
parts.note: a ham is an inept performer, in boxing a poor fighter (a ham-and-egger)
a Dali, a painting by the surrealist Salvador Dali, is famously bizarre to look at

explanation.surface: A poor boxer stands silent, a strange sight to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is ironic: its wordplay calls the answer a poor boxer, while the man himself claimed to be the greatest.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion known as The Greatest, lost to Frazier in 1971, a surreal sight for his fans.

clue.text: See 3
King Edward keeps on rebuffing him

indicators.note: to rebuff is to push back, so the whole assembly is read in reverse

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the word for on goes inside the short name

parts.note: Ed is the short form of the name Edward
re means on or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A king named Edward keeps snubbing some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffing' turns the whole assembly KERED round; 'him' is a fair definition for any man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Derek is a man's first name, so the pronoun him stands for a man of that name.

clue.text: European can start to deal in another continent — here, maybe?

indicators.note: in places the can and the letter inside the continent's name

parts.note: Asia is a continent other than Europe
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the first letter of deal is used

explanation.surface: A European tin can is sent off to trade on another continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the East India Company, a European firm set up to deal in Asia; 'here, maybe' points to East India as one such place of trade.
explanation.definitionFit: East India was the old name for South and Southeast Asia, a likely place for European traders to be.

clue.text: Foremost of athletes shot past

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its first letter, so only the start of athletes is used

parts.note: a shot is a go, a try at something

explanation.surface: The leading athletes sprint past.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means in the past, as in two years ago.

clue.text: Creation of joint Rotary campaign in one town's banks

indicators.note: rotary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards
a bank holds something within it, so the answer is held inside the following words

explanation.surface: The Rotary Club runs a campaign through the banks of a single town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' holds the letters GNINONET inside 'campaign in one town's'; 'Rotary' turns them round. The Rotary Club is a charity, not the mechanism signal it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenoning is cutting a tenon, the tongue that fits a mortise, so it is making a woodworking joint.

clue.text: What 8 19 would shout at him, failing, say, on an exam

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the letters of at him collapse into a new order

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means in say, a cat
re means on or concerning
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Someone would yell at a man flunking an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 19 is the linked answer MUHAMMAD ALI, whose famous boast this was.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali's catchphrase was 'I am the greatest', shouted at opponents and the press.

clue.text: With upward movement of current in dry and wet weather, they'll prevent damp

indicators.note: in a down clue upward means towards the start, so the letter for current climbs earlier in the word for dry

parts.note: arid means dry
I is the symbol for electric current
rains are wet weather

explanation.surface: Rising currents through dry and rainy spells keep a building free of damp.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in ARID moves up one place to give AIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-drains are cavities left around a building's foundations so air circulates and keeps walls dry.

clue.text: See 14
Unable to rise from the canvas surface

definitions.text: Unable to rise from the canvas
definitions.meaning: a boxer who cannot get up off the canvas floor is ...
to surface is to come ..., as in the truth will ...

explanation.surface: A boxer lies flat on the canvas floor of the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A floored boxer counted out is out, and something that comes to light outs.

clue.text: Maniac in a fury boxing learner, so hit below the belt?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase, so the answer is an adverb

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the letter for learner is put inside
a maniac is wild and out of control, so the letters of in a fury run riot

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a learner, from British L-plates

explanation.surface: A furious maniac lays into a novice boxer with low punches.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch below the belt breaks the rules of boxing, so to land one is to hit unfairly.

clue.text: See 8
Showed people responsible for image something hot

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the department in charge of image
an oven is hot

explanation.surface: The publicity team showed off something sizzling.
explanation.definitionFit: Proven is a past participle of prove, and to prove something is to demonstrate or show it.

clue.text: New adherent enthrals grand Epicurean school

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so the letter for grand is held inside
new means made fresh, so the letters of adherent are rearranged

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A new follower is captivated by a fine philosophical school.
explanation.walkthrough: Linked with 4 Down, this is also Madison Square Garden in New York, where the 1971 fight took place.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicurus taught in a garden in Athens, so his followers' school was called The Garden.

clue.text: One's willing to follow crackpot President

indicators.note: following means coming after, so these pieces come after the word for crackpot

parts.note: a crackpot idea is mad
one is I, and 's is is, so I'S becomes IS
on means willing, as in I'm on for it

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to back a crazy president.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth President of the United States; also, Madison Square Garden hosted the 1971 fight.

clue.text: Not 7 you'd pay to see — Spooner's prohibited witches

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: banned means prohibited
hags are witches

explanation.surface: No big fight worth a ticket, says the Spoonerist of some outlawed witches.
explanation.walkthrough: BANNED HAGS with starts swapped gives 'handed bags', heard as HANDBAGS. In British slang 'handbags' is a petty scuffle with much pushing and little punching.
explanation.definitionFit: Handbags is British slang for a minor scuffle, the opposite of the Fight of the Century in 7.

clue.text: Was oddly disposed to feed on dripping?

indicators.note: disposed oddly means set out in an unusual arrangement, so the letters of was are reordered

parts.note: to eat is to feed, the word on simply joining it to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone was strangely inclined to eat beef dripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dripping' looks like the cooking fat in the surface, but it means wet with perspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Asweat means sweating, so someone dripping with perspiration is asweat.

clue.text: Conservative quits

definitions.meaning: ... means even, owing nothing, as in we're quits or all ...

explanation.surface: A Tory politician resigns.
explanation.definitionFit: A square person is conventional, and settling a debt makes two people square, that is even.

clue.text: Army officer restricts lines through focal points

parts.note: a major is an army officer rank
to axe something is to cut it back, so axes means restricts

explanation.surface: An army officer limits the lines passing through key positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'focal points' is the geometry term: the foci of an ellipse.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse's major axis is the longest line across it, passing through both foci; major axes is the plural.

clue.text: See 7
Heading for Uni after a long goodbye

indicators.note: after places the letter behind the other pieces

parts.note: to long for something is to be dying for it, so die means long

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Uni is used

explanation.surface: Bound for university after a long farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for farewell, used in English as a formal goodbye.

clue.text: See 7
But for poor Don King beside 2, contender must hit it!

indicators.note: beside places the king's letter next to the ring's letter

parts.note: bar means except or but for, as in all bar one

indicators.note: poor means shoddy or broken, so the letters of Don are jumbled

parts.note: 2 Down is THE RING, and a ring is shaped like the letter O
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: But for poor Don King at ringside, the boxer would have to land a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Don King was a famous boxing promoter. A barn door is the proverbially easy target: a hopeless fighter 'couldn't hit a barn door'.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn door is a huge target that anyone, even the weakest contender, should manage to hit.

clue.text: Hard sell that executives initially see

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of each of these three words is taken

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city with a see in eastern England

explanation.surface: A tough sales pitch that company bosses first get to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is not the verb but a bishop's diocese; Ely in Cambridgeshire is the crossword's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard as steel, unyielding.
